elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Revised 4.1: "unless terminated upon ninety (90) days written notice by the Company at any time" — an unqualified (no-cause) right for the Company (Customer) to end the Agreement; there is no Order Form construct in this hosting agreement.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Revised 4.1 retains ninety (90) days' written notice for the Company; no 30-day notice appears anywhere in the operative text.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic was inserted. The rationale asserts the Section 3.1 revenue-share (30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month) generates no prepaid fees, but that inapplicability is not established in the rendered operative language, which is silent on refunds.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Revised 4.1 limits HDI (Host/Vendor) to termination "only effective at the expiration of the then-current term," so HDI cannot exit mid-term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Revised 4.1: "terminated upon ninety (90) days written notice by the Company at any time" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band, and "at any time" confirms the right is not confined to the renewal anniversary. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" reflects only the absence of the literal phrase "for convenience"/"without cause"; substantively the right is unconditioned by cause.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Revised 4.2(a): Termination Payment is "the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, divided by two, and (ii) the payments due to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date" — prong (ii) is a hard three-month fee ceiling.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Revised 4.1: "or by HDI only effective at the expiration of the then-current term," replacing the symmetric "by either Party hereto" wording that let HDI pick any date 90+ days out.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The ninety-day requirement is placed ahead of both limbs — "terminated upon ninety (90) days written notice by the Company at any time or by HDI only effective at the expiration of the then-current term" — so it governs an HDI notice as well.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Duplicate checklist string; same operative basis — HDI's termination is expressly "only effective at the expiration of the then-current term."

reasons: Fallback level is complete on the rendered language: Company termination on 90 days' notice at any time, HDI termination only effective at expiry of the then-current term on the same 90 days' notice, and a three-month Section 3.1 fee ceiling on the Termination Payment.

Preferred is correctly not claimed: notice stays at 90 (not 30) days and no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund was added. If the team ever wants the preferred position, it must shorten the Company's notice to thirty (30) days and add a refund sentence (or an express recital that fees are payable only in arrears under Section 3.1).

Minimal: operation 1 edits only the termination limb of the existing renewal sentence and operation 2 keeps the original Net Sales computation as prong (i), so Section 4.2(b)'s zero-or-less netting still produces no payment where trailing twelve-month Net Sales are $800,000 or less. The instalment mechanic in 4.2(c), the Termination Date definition, and the auto-renewal structure are untouched.

Optional clarity repair (not a checklist failure): the revised 4.1 drops "to the other" from "written notice to the other," and never uses the words "for convenience" or "without cause." Consider "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party, which notice may be given by the Company for convenience at any time and by HDI only effective at the expiration of the then-current term" to remove any argument that the notice right is merely a non-renewal right embedded in the automatic-renewal sentence.

The residual point that Section 4.2(a) still bites when the Company terminates for HDI's breach is outside the T4C checklist and is properly raised in the comment rather than drafted in; if pursued, it should be a separate operation carving out termination for cause under Section 1.6.
